Rationale.CS1_Results_vs_Conclusion: All evaluable conclusions in the documentation match the results recorded in the implementation. Key claims about concept lens outperforming raw hidden states for semantic tasks (83.4% vs 39.3% for capital cities), token lens excelling at grammatical tasks (85.4% vs 31.9% for past tense), and rank-256 maintaining performance are all supported by the experimental data. While some numerical approximations in the plan differ slightly from actual values (e.g., past tense token claimed ~65% but achieved 85.4%), these represent underestimates, not contradictions - the directional conclusions remain valid.
Rationale.CS2_Plan_vs_Implementation: All methodology steps from the plan are implemented: (1) Building concept/token lenses by summing OV matrices from top-k heads (implemented in get_ov_sum function), (2) Extracting word embeddings via Llama-2-7b (get_neighbors function), (3) Testing parallelogram arithmetic with nearest-neighbor evaluation (calculate_save_scores), (4) Comparing four settings (raw, concept, token, all) with k=80, and (5) Analyzing effective rank by SVD truncation. All six planned experiments are executed with results stored in the cache directory.
Rationale.CS3_Effect_Size: The reported effects have clearly non-trivial magnitudes. For capital cities, concept lens achieves 83.4% vs raw 39.3% (44.1 percentage point improvement, 112% relative improvement). For past tense, token lens achieves 85.4% vs raw 31.9% (53.5 percentage point improvement, 168% relative improvement). For family relations, concept achieves 51.6% vs raw 19.2% (32.4 percentage points). All improvements are substantial relative to both baseline performance and random chance (~2%), demonstrating robust effect sizes.
Rationale.CS4_Justification: All key design choices are explicitly justified: (1) k=80 heads selected based on prior work by Feucht et al. [2], (2) OV matrix summation justified by mathematical equivalence argument and empirical effectiveness, (3) Task-specific prefixes justified for word disambiguation, (4) Layer selection empirically determined via sweeping, (5) Nearest-neighbor metric follows established word2vec evaluation methodology. Intermediate conclusions about semantic vs surface-level information extraction are supported by success rates exceeding 80% for the primary tasks.
Rationale.CS5_Statistical_Significance: Results are reported without explicit uncertainty estimates or statistical significance information. While sample sizes (n) are recorded in result files and baseline comparisons (random chance, 5-shot ICL) are shown, the project does not report: error bars, confidence intervals, standard errors, statistical tests, or variability from multiple runs. Although the large sample sizes (n>500) and effect sizes make results likely robust, the absence of explicit uncertainty quantification violates the requirement for reporting appropriate measures of statistical significance.
